subject: effect of demographic variables on chi-square fit

messages.author: 6e3bf202055f2791
messages.subject: effect of demographic variables on chi-square fit
parts:
Dear all,
 I have a rather naive question. I searched in many places, but people seem to tend to avoid addressing this issue.

I analyzed some data using lavaan (ofcourse). The model-data fit is excellent even with the strictest criteria like robust chi-square etc. e.g. Robust x2(3)=0.735, p=0.865.
So, this is a great model because it is simple and pseudo-R squared =0.39. Two latent factors predict a binary dependent variable. 

This is the interesting part: However, when I add in the binary regression part of the model another predictor e.g. gender, then the model of the fit becomes much worse, i.e. robust x2(7)=56.97, p<0.0001. I understand that this is an indication that the inclusion of the demographic variables in the model is not needed and the model "complains". The demographic variable gender is not related to the latent factors of the model, becasue when I check the Modificatio Indices they do not have high values. But the pseudo-R squared increases to 0.42 , so it makes some sense to add the variable in the model. 

So my question is: Why does the chi-square increase so much, if the modification indices do not seem to be inflated and if the Rsquared increases (even by a small increase?). 

Also: Should I report the model-fit statistics before adding the demographic variable or after? I have noticed that this happened with many of my datasets.  Any ideas?

Thank you for your time

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: RE: effect of demographic variables on chi-square fit
parts:
Jason—

     I think that your interpretation is off the mark.  You add a variable to the model and DF goes from 3 to 7.  This means that there are 4 additional constraints in the model now, 4 additional parameters which are constrained to values that are not consistent with the data.  It is these constraints that are causing the worsening of chi-square fit.

     Take a look at your modification indices to see where this stress is being felt.  Perhaps these are unexpected constraints, or a syntax error—or maybe they are intentional and motivated by prior knowledge.  The worsening of fit does not mean that the new variables “is not needed.”  If anything, it means that the new variable has more roles to play than you are allowing.

--Ed Rigdon

messages.subject: RE: effect of demographic variables on chi-square fit
parts:
Jason—

Sorry, I missed your remark about your modification indices.  Are you saying that, with a chi-square of 57 (DF = 7), you have no large modification indices?  The evidence should be there in the modification indices.  If it is not, then there are constrained parameters in the model that are being excluded from the modification indices list.

--Ed Rigdon

messages.author: 6e3bf202055f2791
messages.subject: Re: effect of demographic variables on chi-square fit
parts:
Dear all, please allow me to show some information. This is the model

 

   Model1 <- '

        A=~ x1 + x2

        B =~   x3 + x4

        Y ~     A + B

        '

           

     I use this command: fit.m <- lavaan::sem(m, ordered=c(x1, x2, x3, x4), data= d ) 

 

This is the fit:  



  Estimator                                       DWLS      Robust

  Minimum Function Test Statistic                0.222       0.736

  Degrees of freedom                                 3           3

  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.974       0.865

  Scaling correction factor                                  0.558

  Shift parameter                                            0.339

 

 

 

If I add the gender as a predictor of Y and then the fit gets worse

 

   Model2 <- '

        A=~ x1 + x2

        B =~   x3 + x4

        Y ~     A + B + Gender

        '






  Number of observations                          2527
 
  Estimator                                       DWLS      Robust
  Minimum Function Test Statistic               52.089      56.966
  Degrees of freedom                                 7           7
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.000       0.000
  Scaling correction factor                                  0.933
  Shift parameter                                            1.155
    for simple second-order correction (Mplus variant)

 

 

The modification indices are very small. This is strange because the increase of the chi-square cannot be justified if the modification indices are so small.

 

Owever, if I add the gender as a predictor of one of the two latent factors as well, then the model data fit becomes excellent again:

 

   Model3 <- '

        A=~ x1 + x2

        B =~   x3 + x4

        Y ~     A + B + Gender

       A ~~ B

      B ~ Gender

        '

 

  Number of observations                          2527
 
  Estimator                                       DWLS      Robust
  Minimum Function Test Statistic                2.401       4.079
  Degrees of freedom                                 6           6
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.879       0.666
  Scaling correction factor                                  0.727
  Shift parameter                                            0.775

 

 

So, one question is: shouldn’t the modification idices tell me that Gender should be related to one of the latent factors? Also, does Model 3 imply the Gender affects Y directly, but also indirectly through “B ~ Gender”
Thank you for your time
